neighbours.label: the opposing term right after 'but' in a contrast, strongest for a reversed comparative (higher ... but lower)
fire: The new model is faster than the old one but heavier than its main rival.
Turnout was up from the last election but down from the record set in 2008.
His salary is larger than mine but smaller than what the director earns.
The lake is deeper than the pond out back but shallower than the reservoir.
This winter was colder than average but warmer than the one before it.
The second novel sold better than the first but worse than anyone had hoped.
Our team scored more than last season but fewer than the league leaders.
The hotel was cheaper than the one downtown but pricier than the hostel.
quiet: The new model is faster than the old one and lighter than its main rival.
Turnout was up from the last election and also up from the record set in 2008.
His salary is larger than mine and larger than what most teachers earn.
The lake is deeper than the pond out back and much colder in the summer.
This winter was colder than average, with snow arriving early in November.
The second novel sold better than the first and was translated into ten languages.
Our team scored more than last season, mostly thanks to the new striker.
The hotel was cheaper than the one downtown and closer to the train station.

notes: card: ' lower', ' added', ' agreed', ' that' after 'but'/'conceded'; probe: 'higher than last year but lower than 2019' 0.64, other 'but X' continuations 0.08-0.17
